title: Birbal Shortens the Line
text:
The emperor Akbar liked to test the wits of his courtiers with puzzles. One day he took a piece of chalk and drew a straight line across the floor of the court. Then he turned to the assembled nobles and set the challenge: make this line shorter, but without erasing any part of it, and without touching it at all.

The courtiers stared at the line. They walked around it, conferred in low voices, and tried to think of some trick. To make a line shorter, surely you had to rub out part of it. One after another they admitted that it could not be done.

Then Akbar turned to Birbal, his favorite minister, known for his quick mind. Birbal said nothing. He picked up the chalk, bent down, and drew a second line next to the first one, parallel to it and much longer.

Then he stepped back. The emperor's line had not been touched, and not a speck of it had been erased. But beside the new line it was now plainly the shorter of the two. Akbar laughed and praised him, and the courtiers had to admit that Birbal had solved it.
lesson: You do not always have to cut down a rival or a problem to change how it looks. Sometimes the best move is to build something bigger beside it.
caveat: The Akbar and Birbal stories are popular folklore attached to two historical figures, not recorded events.
